q: Attackers are bombarding employees with push-notification MFA prompts at night until someone approves one out of frustration. Which change BEST reduces this risk?
c: Replace push approval with FIDO2 authenticators
Increase the minimum password length to sixteen
Deliver one-time codes over SMS instead of push
Require users to re-enroll their devices monthly

q: A hospital wants access rights assigned through job functions such as nurse or pharmacist, so that transfers between departments only require changing a user's role membership. Which access control model fits BEST?
c: Role-based access control
Discretionary access control
Mandatory access control
Rule-based access control

q: Employees access a partner's cloud application by signing in with corporate credentials through SAML federation. During this flow, which party actually authenticates the user?
c: The partner's application receiving the assertion
The company's identity provider
The SAML assertion exchanged in the flow
The user's web browser handling the redirects

q: An employee who has moved through three departments still holds access granted in every previous role. Which control MOST directly corrects this accumulation?
c: Multi-factor authentication on all accounts
Password rotation every ninety days
Periodic access reviews that recertify entitlements
Single sign-on across enterprise systems

q: In a Kerberos environment, a user authenticates once in the morning and then opens sessions to several servers all day without re-entering a password. Which component makes this possible?
c: The ticket-granting ticket issued by the key distribution center
The server's long-term secret key
The password cached on the workstation
A SAML assertion from the domain controller

q: When comparing biometric door-access systems, a vendor advertises the operating point where the false acceptance rate equals the false rejection rate. What is this metric called?
c: The false acceptance rate
The throughput rate
The failure to enroll rate
The crossover error rate

q: A global firm must let contract reviewers open documents only during business hours, only from managed devices, and only for their assigned region. Which authorization model expresses these conditions MOST naturally?
c: Role-based access control
Attribute-based access control
Mandatory access control
Per-document access control lists

q: A finance employee resigns without notice after a heated dispute with management and leaves the building immediately. From an identity and access management perspective, what should the security team do FIRST?
c: Archive the employee's mailbox and home directory to satisfy data retention requirements
Schedule an exit interview to recover the employee's badge, laptop, and other company assets
Disable all of the employee's accounts, tokens, and remote access immediately
Delete the employee's accounts so that no entitlements remain in any system

q: A security architect must select an authentication design that combines two genuinely different factor categories. Which combination satisfies the requirement for multifactor authentication?
c: A hardware one-time-password token paired with a fingerprint scan
A password paired with answers to preset security questions
A numeric PIN paired with a long passphrase
A fingerprint scan paired with facial recognition

q: A defense contractor's document system assigns classification labels to every file and clearance levels to every user. The operating system enforces the access comparison, and users cannot alter permissions even on files they created themselves. Which access control model is in use?
c: Discretionary access control
Mandatory access control
Role-based access control
Rule-based access control

q: A retailer is building a consumer mobile application backed by REST APIs and wants customers to sign in through external identity providers. The team needs a federation protocol whose tokens the APIs can parse easily on every call. Which choice is MOST appropriate?
c: SAML 2.0 with the HTTP POST browser binding
Kerberos with cross-realm trust between the parties
OAuth 2.0 using the client credentials grant
OpenID Connect issuing signed JSON Web Tokens

q: A network operations team wants centralized AAA for administering routers and switches, including authorization of individual configuration commands and encryption of the entire AAA packet payload between device and server. Which protocol BEST meets these requirements?
c: TACACS+
RADIUS
Diameter
Kerberos

q: An employee moved from accounts payable to procurement three months ago. An audit now finds the employee can both create vendor records and approve payments, a combination policy forbids. Which practice would have BEST prevented this situation?
c: Requiring multifactor authentication for both financial applications
Running an annual recertification campaign across all entitlements
A transfer workflow that revokes prior-role access when an employee changes duties
Applying immediate deprovisioning procedures for terminated employees

q: A colocation facility's server hall is protected by badge readers, but a recent assessment observed employees holding the door open for people behind them. Which control would BEST prevent unauthorized individuals from entering the hall?
c: Monitor the entrance with recorded CCTV coverage
Install an access control vestibule requiring badge and PIN to pass
Deliver security awareness training on tailgating
Review badge logs weekly for entries outside business hours

q: A bank is launching fully online account opening. The security officer notes that strong login controls are useless if a fraudster can enroll under a stolen identity in the first place. Which process addresses this concern?
c: Enrolling every new customer in multifactor authentication
Federating customer logins through a social identity provider
Enforcing strict password length and complexity at registration
Identity proofing that validates evidence such as government-issued documents before enrollment

q: A perimeter firewall evaluates every packet against an ordered list of conditions such as source address, destination port, and protocol, applying the same list to all traffic regardless of who sent it. Which access control model does this illustrate?
c: Rule-based access control
Role-based access control
Discretionary access control
Attribute-based access control

q: After a maintenance window, workstations at a branch office drift more than five minutes from the domain's key distribution center, and Kerberos authentication begins failing with invalid-ticket errors. What security purpose does this strict time requirement serve?
c: It enforces idle session timeout policies consistently across the domain
It ensures X.509 certificate validity periods are evaluated correctly
It keeps password expiration dates synchronized between realms
It bounds ticket lifetimes so captured tickets cannot be replayed later

q: A SaaS provider will let each enterprise customer authenticate its own users through the customer's identity provider and send assertions to the platform. The provider's security manager worries about account takeover. Which concern is MOST important to address in the federation agreements?
c: Customer directories will transmit user passwords to the platform during each login
Weak authentication practices at any customer identity provider become the platform's account-takeover exposure
The customer identity providers will gain the ability to read all data the platform stores
Single sign-on will prevent the platform from generating its own audit logs of user activity

q: An audit finds that 40 system administrators hold standing domain administrator rights, although each uses them only a few times per month. Which approach BEST reduces the associated risk while preserving the team's ability to operate?
c: Rotate the administrators' passwords on a monthly schedule
Consolidate the rights into one shared administrator account
Grant elevated rights just-in-time through a privileged access checkout with time limits
Forward all administrator activity to the SIEM for monitoring

q: A CISO is modernizing the corporate password standard to align with current NIST guidance on memorized secrets. Which change is consistent with that guidance?
c: Screen new passwords against known-compromised lists and drop routine forced expiration
Mandate composition rules requiring all four character classes in every password
Shorten the maximum password age so users must rotate passwords every 30 days
Add knowledge-based security questions as a mandatory secondary verification step

q: Reviewing an authorization design, an architect sees that each subject carries its own list naming the objects it may use and the rights held on each. Auditors complain that answering 'who can access this file?' requires examining every subject in the system. Which statement BEST describes the design?
c: It uses access control lists, which attach permission entries to each object
It uses security labels, which require clearance-to-classification comparison
It uses capability tables, which bind permission entries to each subject
It stores a complete access control matrix with every subject-object pairing

q: A development team proposes letting a new internal portal authenticate users by accepting any valid OAuth 2.0 access token presented to it. During architecture review, the security architect rejects the design. What is the MOST accurate basis for the objection?
c: OAuth cannot be used for federation, so the tokens must be replaced with SAML assertions
An access token conveys delegated authorization, so possessing one does not prove the user's identity
Bearer tokens cannot be replayed when sent over TLS, so the design is already acceptable
The design fails only because the access token lifetime is too long and should be shortened

q: A DevOps review discovers batch jobs that log in with service-account passwords embedded in plaintext within the scripts; the passwords have not changed in four years. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Move the passwords into an encrypted spreadsheet shared with the operations team
Rewrite the jobs to run under each administrator's personal user account
Configure the service accounts to require interactive multifactor authentication
Store the credentials in a secrets vault that rotates them and serves them to jobs via API

q: An intelligence analyst holds a Secret clearance but is denied access to a Secret-classified file belonging to a program she is not assigned to support. Which principle is being applied?
c: Need to know
Least privilege
Separation of duties
Implicit deny

q: A bank's mobile app authenticates customers with a password typed on the phone plus an approval prompt delivered to an authenticator app installed on the same phone. A risk assessment flags the design. What is the MOST significant weakness?
c: Push approval prompts do not qualify as a valid authentication factor
Push notifications travel across the internet and can be read in transit
A compromise of the single device can defeat both factors at once, undermining their independence
Customers must re-enroll the authenticator whenever they replace their phones

q: An enterprise with hundreds of SaaS subscriptions finds that account creation and removal lag weeks behind HR joiner and leaver events. The IAM team wants an open standard to automate provisioning and deprovisioning from the central directory to the SaaS providers. Which should they adopt?
c: SCIM
SAML 2.0
OAuth 2.0
LDAP

q: While engineering roles for a new ERP system, the design team must guarantee that no single user can ever hold the ability both to create a vendor and to approve payments to that vendor. Which mechanism BEST enforces this within the authorization model?
c: Dual control requiring two people to jointly execute payment approvals
Job rotation moving staff between procurement positions periodically
Least privilege provisioning of each user's individual entitlements
Mutually exclusive role constraints so the two roles can never be assigned to one user

q: A CIO proposes enterprise-wide single sign-on to reduce helpdesk password resets and user friction. The CISO supports the project but insists a specific risk be mitigated first. Which risk is MOST significant with SSO?
c: Users will need to remember more passwords, encouraging weak choices
One compromised credential or session can open every connected application
Single sign-on is incompatible with multifactor authentication
Application owners lose the ability to log the actions of signed-on users

q: During a quarterly review, an analyst discovers an enabled account belonging to a contractor whose engagement ended six months ago. The account's last successful logon was three days ago. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Delete the account to eliminate the exposure permanently
Perform root cause analysis of the deprovisioning control failure
Disable the account and preserve it while the recent activity is investigated
Contact the contractor's former sponsor to confirm the engagement status

q: A trading firm plans to roll out fingerprint authentication. The privacy officer asks the architect to explain the MOST important way biometric credentials differ from passwords when designing storage and breach response. Which response is accurate?
c: Biometric matching is exact, so stored templates require no special protection
A compromised biometric cannot be reissued, so template protection and fallback revocation options are essential
Fingerprints are classified as something you have, so adding a PIN provides no additional factor
Templates are stored as one-way hashes, so their disclosure creates no meaningful risk

q: A government agency issues employees smart cards containing a private key, and each user must enter a PIN to unlock the card before it will perform authentication. Which BEST characterizes this scheme?
c: Single-factor authentication, because the PIN is the actual credential
Two-factor authentication combining something you are with something you know
Single-factor authentication until a fingerprint reader is added to the card
Two-factor authentication combining possession of the card with knowledge of the PIN

q: In a centralized attribute-based access control deployment, an application gateway intercepts each user request, forwards the request context to a central policy engine, receives a permit or deny verdict, and then allows or blocks the request. In this architecture, what is the gateway?
c: The policy enforcement point
The policy decision point
The policy administration point
The policy information point

q: A junior engineer reviewing a new application's authorization module notices that when a user's request does not match any configured permission rule, the application grants the access and merely logs a warning. Which access control principle is the application violating?
c: Least privilege
Separation of duties
Implicit deny
Defense in depth

q: During a design review for a new customer portal, the security architect is asked how account passwords should be protected in the credential database. Which approach BEST protects the passwords against offline cracking if the database is stolen?
c: Hash each password with a unique salt using a deliberately slow adaptive function such as bcrypt or a memory-hard function such as Argon2
Encrypt all passwords with AES-256 using a key stored in a hardware security module
Hash all passwords with a single fast cryptographic hash such as SHA-256 to preserve performance
Require all passwords to be at least sixteen characters so that cracking becomes impractical

q: An audit finds that 14 employees who left the company during the past year still had active directory accounts because their managers forgot to submit termination tickets. Which remediation BEST prevents this failure from recurring?
c: Require all managers to complete annual training on the termination checklist
Integrate the directory with the HR system so employment status changes automatically trigger account deprovisioning
Increase the frequency of user access reviews from annually to quarterly
Configure all accounts to expire automatically every 90 days unless renewed

q: Incident responders determine that attackers extracted the secret of the Kerberos key distribution center's krbtgt account and have been forging ticket-granting tickets for arbitrary users. Password resets for all user accounts have already been completed. What MUST the team do to invalidate the forged tickets?
c: Reduce the maximum ticket-granting ticket lifetime so the forged tickets expire much sooner
Force all users to re-authenticate so that fresh session keys are issued to everyone
Rebuild every domain controller in the forest from known-good installation media
Reset the krbtgt account credential twice so no ticket signed with the stolen secret is honored

q: A company federates workforce access to 40 SaaS applications through its identity provider. During a control test, an account disabled at the identity provider could still use several SaaS applications for many hours afterward. Which control gap MOST likely explains this?
c: The SaaS providers are caching user passwords locally instead of deferring to the identity provider
The federation trust uses weak certificate key lengths that allow assertions to be forged
The applications rely on long-lived sessions and tokens with no revocation or logout propagation from the identity provider
The deprovisioning workflow failed to remove the user's role assignments inside each application

q: A hardware vendor's technician needs one-time access to a server room to replace a failed drive under warranty. Which approach BEST controls this physical access?
c: Issue the technician a temporary badge carrying the same access profile as data-center staff
Log the visit and have an authorized employee escort the technician for the entire time on site
Have the technician sign a nondisclosure agreement before being allowed to enter the room
Verify the technician's government identification at reception and then allow unescorted access

q: A bank uses SMS one-time codes as the second factor for customer logins. Fraud investigators report a spike in account takeovers in which attackers ported victims' phone numbers to new SIM cards. What is the BEST strategic response?
c: Migrate customers to an authenticator app or hardware token so codes no longer travel over the carrier network
Increase the length of the SMS one-time code from six digits to eight digits
Require customers to change their online banking passwords more frequently
Shorten the validity window of each SMS one-time code to thirty seconds

q: A finance application allows a user to hold both the 'create payment' and 'approve payment' roles, but the system blocks any user from approving a payment that they themselves created. Which control is being applied?
c: Static separation of duties enforced at role assignment
Least privilege enforced through role-based access control
Two-person integrity requiring simultaneous action by two employees
Dynamic separation of duties enforced at transaction time

q: Quarterly access recertifications show a 99.8 percent approval rate, and sampling reveals managers approving hundreds of entitlements within minutes, including several later confirmed to be inappropriate. As the IAM program lead, what is the BEST improvement to make?
c: Move the recertification campaigns from quarterly to monthly so inappropriate access is caught sooner
Give reviewers risk-ranked, plain-language entitlement descriptions with peer-group outlier flags, and require justification for high-risk approvals
Reassign the review responsibility from business managers to the security operations team
Automatically revoke any entitlement the reviewer has not explicitly approved by the campaign deadline

q: An enterprise deploys IEEE 802.1X port-based network access control. A laptop's supplicant submits credentials that are carried through the wired switch to a central server. In this architecture, which component actually decides whether the laptop is granted network access?
c: The authentication server that evaluates the credentials against the identity store
The switch acting as the authenticator on the access port
The supplicant software running on the connecting laptop
The DHCP server that issues the laptop its network configuration

q: An agency is designing digital identity requirements for three online services: viewing public park hours, filing personal tax information, and approving high-value grant disbursements. The CISO rejects a proposal to require in-person identity proofing and hardware authenticators for all three. Which principle supports the CISO's position?
c: Defense in depth requires layered controls rather than strong authentication alone
Usability must always take precedence over security in citizen-facing services
Identity and authenticator assurance levels should be selected per service based on the risk and impact of a failure
Strong authentication is unnecessary because the sensitive services already encrypt data in transit

q: A project manager creates a folder on the collaboration platform and personally decides which colleagues receive read or edit rights, adding and removing people as she sees fit. Which access control model is the platform implementing?
c: Mandatory access control
Discretionary access control
Role-based access control
Attribute-based access control

q: A hospital maintains a 'break-glass' administrator account so clinicians and engineers can obtain emergency access if the identity system fails during a patient-safety event. Which set of controls BEST governs this account?
c: Disable the account entirely and require the on-call director to create a fresh one during each emergency
Distribute the account password to all senior staff so that an emergency never delays access
Protect the account with the same multifactor authentication required for routine administrator logins
Store the credential sealed, alert on any use, and review then rotate it after every activation

q: A red team reports that any authenticated domain user can request Kerberos service tickets for accounts with registered service principal names and crack the encrypted tickets offline, recovering several service-account passwords. What is the MOST effective remediation?
c: Replace the vulnerable accounts with managed service accounts or long, random, machine-generated passwords
Configure account lockout to block accounts after a small number of failed logon attempts
Restrict the ability to request service tickets to members of a dedicated service operators group
Shorten the service ticket lifetime so that any cracked ticket expires within a few hours

q: Auditors find that six database administrators all log in to production servers using one shared 'dbadmin' account, making it impossible to attribute changes to individuals. Which remediation BEST restores accountability?
c: Require the shared password to be changed every 30 days and immediately after any administrator departs
Enable verbose logging of every command executed under the shared dbadmin account
Issue each administrator a unique privileged account requiring elevation, and remove direct shared logins
Require administrators to record each use of dbadmin in a sign-out spreadsheet

q: During a penetration test of a SAML-federated procurement portal, testers modify the username inside an intercepted assertion, replay it to the service provider, and are logged in as the altered user. What is the ROOT cause of this vulnerability?
c: The identity provider issued the assertion over an unencrypted transport channel
The service provider fails to properly validate the digital signature covering the assertion
The assertion validity lifetime is too long, allowing it to be replayed after it should have expired
The identity provider did not require multifactor authentication before issuing the assertion

q: A retail website lets customers reset forgotten passwords by answering their mother's maiden name and the name of their first pet. Why is this design considered weak?
c: The answers are too difficult for legitimate customers to remember accurately over time
Security questions count as a biometric factor and therefore can never be changed
The reset process fails to notify customers by email whenever it has been used
The answers are often discoverable from social media and public records, so they rest on knowledge attackers can obtain

q: A managed services provider needs system accounts for a nine-month implementation project. Historically, similar third-party accounts have remained active for years after their projects ended. Which provisioning practice BEST addresses this risk?
c: Create the accounts with expiration dates tied to the contract end and require a named sponsor to renew them
Grant the provider one shared account so there is only a single credential to remember to remove
Add the provider's accounts to the population covered by the quarterly access review
Require the provider to commit contractually to reporting its staff departures promptly

q: A network capture during an internal assessment shows several applications sending user credentials to the corporate directory as LDAP simple binds in cleartext. What should the security team require?
c: Replace the directory service entirely with a Kerberos key distribution center
Move the directory server into a separate VLAN so packet captures become harder
Require LDAPS or StartTLS so that all binds occur over an encrypted channel
Hash each password on the client before it is sent in the bind request

q: A global firm wants stronger login security, but the workforce complains that entering a one-time code at every single login is burdensome. Which authentication strategy BEST balances risk reduction and user friction?
c: Drop the second factor entirely for all users and compensate by forcing password changes every 30 days
Adopt risk-based authentication that steps up to additional factors only when signals such as device, location, or behavior look anomalous
Require the one-time code only for administrators and IT staff, exempting the general workforce from a second factor
Extend the session and token lifetimes so that each user only has to authenticate about once per month

q: Five years after deploying role-based access control, an enterprise has 11,000 roles for 9,000 employees; many roles have a single member, and administrators create a new role for nearly every access request. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Run a role engineering effort combining top-down business analysis with bottom-up entitlement mining to consolidate roles, using attributes for exceptions
Freeze all new role creation immediately and maintain the freeze until the total role count falls below the number of employees
Abandon the role model entirely and grant all future access through direct, individual user-level permission assignments
Migrate every existing role unchanged into a new identity governance platform so the roles can at least be centrally reported

q: A terminated engineer's network accounts were disabled within minutes, yet he entered the office with his badge three days later because the physical access system is administered separately by the facilities team. What is the BEST long-term correction?
c: Post security guards at every entrance to visually verify that each entrant is a current employee
Require the facilities team to reconcile the badge holder list against HR records once each month
Shorten badge validity so that every employee badge must be re-enabled at reception each week
Manage badge credentials through the same identity lifecycle processes that drive logical account deprovisioning

q: Employees connecting to corporate Wi-Fi have had credentials harvested by rogue access points broadcasting the corporate network name. The current design uses username and password over a protocol where clients frequently ignore server certificate warnings. What is the BEST fix?
c: Hide the SSID broadcast and filter wireless connections by client MAC address
Deploy certificate-based mutual authentication such as EAP-TLS so clients verify the network before presenting anything
Require employees to change their Wi-Fi passwords whenever a rogue access point is detected nearby
Increase the wireless encryption strength from AES-128 to AES-256 on all corporate access points

q: A mid-sized company plans to move all workforce authentication to a cloud identity-as-a-service provider fronting every business application. From a risk-management perspective, which consideration is MOST important to evaluate before committing?
c: Whether the provider's login interface can be rebranded with the company's logo and color scheme
Whether the provider supports importing the company's existing password hashes during migration
The provider's availability history, contractual service levels, and the company's contingency plan if the service is unreachable
Whether the per-user subscription cost is lower than operating the current on-premises directory

q: After enabling a policy that locks accounts for 24 hours after three failed logins, a trading firm suffers an attack in which someone deliberately fails logins against hundreds of known usernames, locking most traders out during market hours. Which redesign BEST balances the competing risks?
c: Keep the hard lockout policy in place but reduce the lockout duration from 24 hours to one hour
Remove the failed-login limit entirely and rely on password complexity rules to resist guessing attacks
Suppress all username hints and error details so attackers cannot confirm which accounts actually exist
Replace hard lockout with progressive delays and risk-based blocking of suspicious sources, backed by MFA and monitoring

q: A data center manager discovers the server room is secured only by mechanical keyed locks, with copies of the key held by a dozen staff. After an unexplained after-hours entry, no one can determine who opened the door. Which control BEST addresses this accountability gap?
c: Install a high-security cipher lock and share the combination only with senior staff
Re-key the door and sharply reduce the number of physical keys that are issued
Deploy an electronic badge access system that logs each individual's entry events
Add CCTV camera coverage of the corridor leading to the server room door

q: A red team clones several employees' 125 kHz proximity badges using a concealed reader in an elevator and later enters a restricted lab. Physical security asks how to prevent recurrence. Which measure BEST addresses the root cause?
c: Migrate to smart cards that perform encrypted mutual authentication with the door readers
Shorten badge validity periods so that any cloned credentials expire much sooner
Install CCTV at the lab entrance so unauthorized entrants can be detected and identified
Require employees to carry their badges in shielded sleeves whenever off duty

q: An organization keeps monthly full-backup tapes in an on-site media library. An audit notes that any IT staff member can walk in and remove tapes without any record being made. Which control BEST governs access to these data assets?
c: Encrypt every backup tape so that any media removed from the library cannot be read
Contract an off-site vaulting provider and relocate all of the backup tapes there
Replace the tape library entirely with disk-based backups inside the data center
Require logged check-in/check-out of tapes, authorized by a designated media custodian

q: A biometric iris scanner will control the sole entrance to a facility housing classified prototypes. The integrator asks the security manager how the matching threshold should be set. From a security standpoint, what is the BEST guidance?
c: Set the threshold at the crossover error rate so both error types are balanced
Tune toward the lowest achievable false acceptance rate, accepting more false rejections
Tune toward the lowest false rejection rate so authorized personnel are never delayed
Loosen the enrollment capture-quality requirements to reduce the failure-to-enroll rate

q: A trading firm finds that staff sometimes leave terminals unlocked and colleagues have executed trades on those unattended sessions within moments of the trader stepping away. Login already requires strong MFA. Which approach BEST mitigates session takeover after the initial login?
c: Require a hardware security key at every login to further strengthen initial authentication
Shorten the inactivity timeout so any unattended session locks itself sooner
Increase password complexity and rotation requirements for the trading applications
Deploy continuous authentication on behavioral traits such as keystroke dynamics, challenging the session on anomalies

q: Nurses share mobile workstations and frequently walk away mid-task, leaving patient records open under the previous user's session. Which measure BEST balances security with clinical workflow?
c: Short inactivity timeouts combined with fast badge-tap re-authentication for returning users
A shared generic ward login so open records are never attributed to an individual nurse
Longer session lifetimes with one mandatory logout at the end of every nursing shift
Full password entry plus an MFA prompt every single time any patient chart is opened

q: Attackers phone a company's help desk posing as executives who lost their phones, persuade agents to enroll new MFA authenticators for the accounts, and then take them over. No passwords were ever compromised. Which change MOST directly addresses the exploited weakness?
c: Replace app-based authenticators with phishing-resistant hardware security keys
Have agents verify callers by quizzing them on employment details held in the HR system
Require identity proofing comparable to initial enrollment before binding any replacement authenticator
Force an immediate password reset across all executive accounts after the incident

q: System administrators at a firm each use a single account holding domain administrator rights for all activity, including email, web browsing, and routine office tasks. Which practice should the security manager mandate?
c: Move the administrators onto one shared admin account protected by a much stronger password
Issue each administrator separate standard and privileged accounts, using the privileged one only for admin tasks
Require multifactor authentication whenever the administrators read their corporate email
Limit each administrator to local administrator rights on their own assigned workstation

q: A university federates with a cloud research service via SAML. The service only needs to know a user is current faculty, but the identity provider's default configuration releases full name, national ID number, and department to every relying party. What should the identity architect do?
c: Encrypt the SAML assertions so the attributes cannot be read while they are in transit
Have the service sign a data processing agreement covering the released attributes
Replace SAML with OpenID Connect, since it shares fewer user attributes by default
Configure per-relying-party attribute release limited to an affiliation or entitlement claim

q: A banking consortium wants customers to prove employment or account standing to third parties without the verifier contacting the issuing bank each time, and with the customer choosing which claims to disclose in each interaction. Which identity model BEST fits these goals?
c: Decentralized identity with cryptographically verifiable credentials held in a user-controlled wallet
A central OAuth authorization server that issues scoped access tokens to each verifier
SAML federation in which each third-party verifier becomes a relying party of the bank's IdP
An enterprise directory whose records are synchronized out to each verifier using SCIM

q: A SaaS provider supports both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML single sign-on. Its security architect observes that one flow forces the service to accept assertions it never asked for. Which statement BEST captures the risk-based guidance?
c: IdP-initiated SSO is safer because the IdP always authenticates the user before any assertion is ever sent to the service
Prefer SP-initiated SSO, because unsolicited IdP-initiated assertions cannot be matched to a request the SP generated, easing injection and replay
The two flows carry identical risk because the assertions are digitally signed by the IdP in either flow
IdP-initiated SSO should be preferred because it eliminates the redirect step that an attacker could otherwise tamper with

q: HR clerks need to look up employee office locations and reporting managers but must never see salary or health fields stored in the same employee records. Which authorization approach MOST directly enforces this requirement?
c: Context-dependent access control evaluating the time, location, and device of each query
Role-based access control granting the clerks an HR role with rights on the employee table
Content-dependent access control that exposes only permitted fields, such as restricted database views
Field-level encryption applied to the salary and health columns in the database

q: Warehouse workers use handheld scanner applications that display only the three menu functions their job requires; all other functions are hidden or greyed out and are also rejected by the server. Which access control concept does this illustrate?
c: A constrained user interface that restricts the functions available to the user
Attribute-based access control evaluating user and environmental attributes per request
A capability list enumerating the objects and rights held by each warehouse worker
Security through obscurity, because the unavailable functions are merely being hidden

q: An audit at a bank finds users gaining access to sensitive shares through chains of five or more nested directory groups, and no administrator can state what a given user can effectively reach. Which remediation BEST restores manageable authorization?
c: Assign permissions directly to individual user accounts to eliminate all group ambiguity
Increase how often managers recertify each user's directly assigned group memberships
Migrate the sensitive file shares to mandatory access control with classification labels
Impose group governance limiting nesting depth, assigning an owner per group, and reviewing effective access

q: Regional IT help desks need only to reset passwords and unlock accounts for users in their own region, yet today every help desk technician holds full domain administrator rights. What is the BEST correction?
c: Enroll the technicians in a PAM vault that records every domain administrator session they open
Create delegated administration roles scoped to reset and unlock rights over each region's user accounts
Require dual authorization from a second technician before any password reset is performed
Rotate the domain administrator credentials automatically at the end of every help desk shift

q: An internal workflow tool integrates with the corporate email platform through OAuth. Developers registered it to request the full-mailbox-access scope even though the tool only sends notification messages. What should the security reviewer require?
c: Switch the integration to the client credentials grant so no user consent screens appear
Store the integration's refresh token inside the enterprise secrets management vault
Re-register the application for the narrowest scope that permits sending mail only
Shorten the access token lifetime so the broad scope expires much more quickly

q: A payroll specialist who left the company two years ago is rehired into a marketing role. The IT team proposes reactivating her archived account to save setup time. What should the identity management lead direct?
c: Provision a fresh set of entitlements through the standard joiner process for the new role
Reactivate the account but require a password reset and new MFA enrollment before first login
Reactivate the account and flag it for scrutiny during the next quarterly recertification
Provision a new account while leaving the old one active to preserve access to historical data

q: New hires automatically receive access to over forty applications on day one because the onboarding template has grown for years as departments added useful systems. Recertification campaigns keep flagging large volumes of unused entitlements. What is the BEST structural fix?
c: Deploy automation that revokes any entitlement that has gone unused for ninety consecutive days
Shorten the recertification campaign cycle for these entitlements from annual to quarterly
Require each new hire's manager to review and approve the full onboarding template individually
Cut birthright access to a minimal common baseline and grant the remainder through role-based or approved requests

q: During access recertification for a finance data warehouse, line managers approve their staff's access but admit they do not know what the data contains or who should legitimately use it. Who is BEST positioned to certify access to this data set?
c: The database administrator, who understands the schema, grants, and permission structures
The finance data owner, who is accountable for the data and its authorized business uses
The chief information security officer, as the senior executive accountable for security
Each user's line manager, because they know their own employees' current job duties

q: A cloud security review finds thousands of service accounts, API keys, and workload identities; many have no identifiable owner, and several belonged to projects cancelled years ago. Which action should the IAM program take FIRST?
c: Rotate every discovered credential immediately to invalidate any copies already stolen
Migrate all of the service accounts into the enterprise secrets vault for central control
Build an inventory of the non-human identities with assigned owners and lifecycle status before remediating
Delete every account that shows no authentication activity within the past twelve months

q: Departing employees keep appearing as active users in several SaaS tools that business units purchased directly on corporate cards; none of the tools are connected to the corporate IdP or provisioning system. Which response BEST addresses the root cause?
c: Mandate SSO and provisioning integration as a purchase condition for SaaS, with ongoing discovery of unsanctioned apps
Add the SaaS tools identified so far to the manual offboarding checklist used by the service desk
Prohibit business units from purchasing any software outside the central IT procurement process
Extend the quarterly user access review campaigns to cover each of the discovered SaaS applications

q: A native mobile app receives OAuth authorization codes through a custom URL scheme. Security testing shows that a malicious app on the same device could register the identical scheme and intercept the returned code. Which control MOST directly mitigates this interception?
c: Use the implicit grant so that no authorization code is ever exposed on the device
Embed a confidential client secret in the mobile app to authenticate its token requests
Prompt the user to re-enter their credentials at the moment the code is redeemed for tokens
Implement PKCE so redeeming the code requires the code verifier that only the initiating app holds

q: During a purple-team exercise, testers compromise a legacy application server configured for unconstrained Kerberos delegation and harvest forwarded TGTs for every user who connected, including domain administrators. Which remediation BEST reduces this exposure?
c: Enforce substantially shorter Kerberos ticket lifetimes across the entire domain
Replace unconstrained delegation with constrained or resource-based delegation limited to the required services
Move the legacy application server into a separately administered Kerberos realm
Mandate smart card logon for every account that holds domain administrator rights

q: A penetration tester obtains a valid ID token issued by the corporate OpenID Connect provider to a low-security internal app, then presents it to the HR portal, which accepts it and establishes a session. The token's signature verifies correctly. What is the underlying flaw?
c: The identity provider's private signing key must have been compromised by the tester
The HR portal should have demanded an OAuth access token rather than an ID token
The HR portal fails to validate the audience claim, so tokens minted for other clients are accepted
The token lifetime is configured too long, allowing it to be replayed to a second application

q: A company enforces MFA on its cloud email portal, yet an attacker using password spraying gains mailbox access with passwords alone. Logs show the successful logins arrived through an IMAP basic-authentication endpoint. What should the security team do FIRST?
c: Disable legacy authentication protocols that cannot enforce the MFA policy, after identifying dependent clients
Strengthen the password composition and complexity requirements to defeat spraying attempts
Deploy stronger multifactor methods, such as hardware security keys, for all mailbox users
Block sign-in attempts originating from countries where the company has no business presence

q: A security manager installs cameras covering the entrances to a records storage room. The cameras record continuously, and footage is reviewed only after an incident is reported; nobody monitors the feeds in real time. Which control category BEST describes this CCTV deployment?
c: Preventive control
Deterrent control
Detective control
Corrective control

q: During security awareness training, a new analyst asks why typing a username at a login prompt is not enough to be granted access, since the system then 'knows who they are.' Which concept explains what supplying a username actually accomplishes?
c: Identification - the user asserts an identity that has not yet been proven
Authentication - the system has verified that the user is who they claim to be
Authorization - the system has determined what resources the user may access
Accountability - the system can now reliably attribute actions to the user

q: A facilities team connects a new building-automation controller to the corporate network. The installation guide, freely downloadable from the vendor's website, lists the administrator username and password that every unit ships with. What should the security team require FIRST before the device goes live?
c: Place the controller on an isolated VLAN behind a dedicated firewall
Change the default administrative credentials to unique, strong replacements
Enable detailed logging of all administrative access to the device
Verify that the controller is running the latest vendor firmware version

q: An employee is approved for a six-month unpaid sabbatical and is expected to return to the same role. What is the BEST way to handle the employee's user account during the absence?
c: Delete the account and provision a brand-new identity when the employee returns
Leave the account active but force a password change before the employee departs
Transfer the account credentials to the employee's manager to cover urgent tasks
Disable the account, retain its data and entitlements, and re-enable it upon verified return

q: A phishing investigation reveals that many employees reuse a single memorized password across dozens of external business websites that cannot be integrated with the company's SSO. Which measure would BEST reduce this credential-reuse risk?
c: Enforce stricter password complexity rules on all corporate systems
Require employees to change their passwords every 60 days
Deploy an enterprise password manager that generates and stores unique credentials per site
Block employee access to external websites that are not integrated with corporate SSO

q: During design review of a new data center, the security architect wants all electronic door locks to remain locked whenever power is lost, but the fire marshal objects with respect to the emergency exit doors. How should this conflict be resolved?
c: Configure egress doors to fail-safe (unlock) on power loss and add compensating controls such as alarms, guards, and cameras
Keep all doors fail-secure because protecting the assets inside is the facility's primary mission
Install uninterruptible power for the locks so a power loss never actually occurs
Compromise by configuring half of the egress doors fail-secure and the other half fail-safe

q: Employees connect through a VPN, and once connected they can reach nearly every internal application. After a stolen laptop with cached VPN credentials was used to roam the network, the CISO wants a strategy that no longer grants broad access simply for being 'inside.' Which approach BEST meets this goal?
c: Add a second authentication factor to the VPN login process
Adopt a zero trust model that authorizes each application request based on user identity, device posture, and context
Perform a network access control health check on every endpoint before admitting it to the network
Divide the internal network into multiple VLANs separated by internal firewalls

q: A software vendor must connect remotely each month to maintain a hospital's critical clinical system. The contract requires the hospital to be able to demonstrate exactly what the vendor's engineers did during each maintenance window. Which control BEST satisfies this requirement?
c: Have the vendor sign a nondisclosure and acceptable-use agreement before each maintenance window
Require the vendor's engineers to authenticate with multifactor authentication
Review the clinical system's native event logs after each maintenance window
Route vendor connections through a privileged access gateway that records the full interactive session

q: A company is selecting a biometric system for its main employee entrance, where about 4,000 people arrive during a 45-minute morning peak. Two shortlisted products have nearly identical crossover error rates and similar pricing. Which factor should MOST influence the final selection?
c: The false acceptance rate each product achieves at its default threshold setting
Verification speed and how willingly employees will accept using the modality
The storage size of each product's biometric template in the database
The physiological uniqueness of the trait each modality measures

q: During a red-team exercise, testers unlocked several employees' tablets by holding printed photographs of the device owners in front of the facial recognition camera. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Require facial recognition that performs presentation attack (liveness) detection such as depth and motion analysis
Raise the matching threshold so the algorithm demands a much closer facial match
Re-enroll all employees to capture higher-resolution reference templates
Increase the lockout penalty after failed facial recognition attempts

q: To cut help-desk calls, an IT director proposes password synchronization so each user's single password is replicated to the mainframe, the ERP system, and several legacy applications with widely varying security postures. What is the MOST significant risk of this approach?
c: Users will still have to log in to each application separately, so convenience will not improve much
The synchronized environment becomes single sign-on and inherits SSO session hijacking risks
A compromise of the weakest participating system exposes a password that is valid on every system
Replication delays after each password change will repeatedly lock users out of some applications

q: A retailer plans to let employees of a new logistics partner access its shipment portal through federated login using the partner's identity provider. Before any technical integration work begins, what should the retailer do FIRST?
c: Exchange SAML metadata and token-signing certificates with the partner's engineers
Conduct a penetration test of the partner's identity provider infrastructure
Require the partner to enforce multifactor authentication for all portal users
Negotiate a federation agreement defining required assurance levels, liabilities, and attribute handling

q: Enterprise single sign-on failed for four hours when the token-signing certificate on the identity provider expired unnoticed. Which measure BEST prevents a recurrence?
c: Implement certificate lifecycle management with expiry monitoring and staged key rollover published in federation metadata
Issue the replacement signing certificate with a much longer validity period
Configure relying applications to accept assertions signed with an expired certificate during a grace period
Switch the identity provider to a self-signed signing certificate that the organization fully controls

q: A finance department depends on a 20-year-old application that supports only its own built-in username and password form and cannot be modified. The IAM program requires every application to sit behind enterprise SSO with MFA. What is the BEST way to bring this application into compliance?
c: Rewrite the application to natively support OpenID Connect before the program deadline
Front the application with an SSO gateway that enforces modern authentication and then injects vaulted credentials into the legacy login form
Synchronize the application's local passwords with the enterprise directory
Exempt the application and compensate with a stronger password policy for its local accounts

q: An identity governance rollout stalls because the provisioning engine receives conflicting values for employees' departments, managers, and job codes from the HR system, the ERP directory, and a legacy phone directory. What should the IAM team do to resolve this?
c: Configure the engine to accept whichever source updated each attribute most recently
Let employees review and correct their own profile attributes through a self-service portal
Designate an authoritative source for each attribute and synchronize all other systems from it
Have the help desk manually reconcile conflicting records as provisioning errors are reported

q: An internal audit finds that many entitlements in the ERP system were granted directly by IT administrators after informal chat messages, with no record of who authorized the access. Which change BEST addresses the audit finding?
c: Require administrators to record the requester's name in the ticket queue after granting access
Run a one-time cleanup removing entitlements that nobody can currently explain
Restrict ERP entitlement changes to a smaller group of the most senior administrators
Route all access requests through a workflow requiring documented approval from the resource owner before provisioning occurs

q: A penetration test showed that SQL injection in a customer portal yielded complete control of the database because the web application connects using an account holding database administrator rights. Beyond fixing the injection flaw itself, which access control change is MOST important?
c: Reconnect the application through a dedicated account limited to the specific tables and procedures it needs
Store the application's database password in a secrets vault with automatic rotation
Deploy a web application firewall in front of the customer portal
Encrypt the customer database using transparent data encryption

q: A DevOps team's build pipeline authenticates to the cloud provider using API keys created three years ago and stored in the pipeline's configuration. A cloud security review flags the keys as a critical finding. Which remediation BEST eliminates this class of risk?
c: Move the API keys into a secrets manager and rotate them automatically every 24 hours
Establish workload identity federation so pipeline jobs exchange signed platform identity tokens for short-lived cloud credentials
Encrypt the pipeline configuration files that currently contain the API keys
Restrict the API keys so they are accepted only from the build platform's IP address ranges

q: Attackers tried the password 'Autumn2026!' exactly once against every account in a company's cloud email tenant and successfully logged in to nine mailboxes. Account lockout was configured at five failed attempts. Which control would MOST effectively have prevented these compromises?
c: Reducing the account lockout threshold from five failed attempts to three
Requiring all users to change their passwords every 45 days
Enforcing phishing-resistant multifactor authentication on all logins
Increasing the minimum password length from eight characters to twelve

q: A strategy consulting firm serves two competing pharmaceutical clients. Compliance requires that once a consultant opens either client's deal documents, that consultant must automatically be barred from ever opening the competitor's documents. Which access control model is designed for this requirement?
c: Role-based access control with mutually exclusive client roles assigned at hiring
Mandatory access control using sensitivity labels and clearances
Discretionary access control with owner-managed ACLs on each client's folder
The Brewer-Nash model, which restricts access dynamically based on the subject's access history

q: A departing engineer's directory account was disabled on their last day, yet three weeks later VPN logs show new successful connections attributed to that engineer. The VPN concentrator authenticates users solely by client certificates issued from the corporate CA. What gap in the deprovisioning process MOST likely allowed this?
c: The leaver process never revoked the engineer's client certificate, which the VPN continued accepting independently of the directory
The VPN session timeout allowed an existing session to remain connected for three weeks after the disablement
The directory disablement had not yet replicated to the domain controller consulted by the VPN
The engineer's account was disabled rather than deleted, leaving the identity available for reuse

q: Forensic analysis confirms that attackers exfiltrated the database in which an authentication server stores the shared secret seeds for all employees' TOTP soft tokens. Passwords were not exposed. What must the organization do to restore the integrity of its multifactor authentication?
c: Force an immediate password reset for every employee account
Revoke all existing tokens and re-enroll every user with newly generated seeds
Shorten the TOTP code validity window from 60 seconds to 30 seconds
Temporarily block logins from unrecognized locations until the investigation concludes

q: An architect discovers that RADIUS authentication traffic between branch-office network access servers and the central data center crosses a third-party WAN. The review notes that RADIUS obfuscates only the User-Password attribute, leaving usernames, accounting data, and other attributes readable in transit. Which remediation BEST protects this traffic?
c: Replace the shared secrets on all RADIUS clients with much longer random values
Migrate the branch network devices from RADIUS to TACACS+
Tunnel the RADIUS exchanges over TLS (RadSec) or an IPsec VPN between the sites
Enable RADIUS accounting so that any interception attempts generate log entries

q: A bank's corporate customers authenticate to the payment portal with passwords plus hardware OTP tokens, yet fraud continues: banking malware on customer PCs waits for a legitimate login and then silently submits wire transfers inside the authenticated session. Which control BEST addresses this fraud?
c: Require customers to enter a second OTP code at the start of every portal session
Deploy continuous behavioral biometrics to detect account takeover during active sessions
Reduce the portal's idle session timeout from thirty minutes to five minutes
Require out-of-band confirmation on a separate device that displays each transfer's payee and amount for approval

q: Domain administrators already use separate privileged accounts, yet investigators find attackers captured those credentials with a keylogger delivered by a phishing email opened on an administrator's everyday workstation - the same machine used for domain administration. Which control BEST prevents recurrence?
c: Issue dedicated, hardened privileged access workstations used exclusively for administrative tasks
Require administrators to reach servers through a jump host from their everyday workstations
Shorten the rotation interval for all privileged account passwords
Deploy endpoint detection and response agents on the administrators' workstations

q: During a penetration test, the team extracts crackable authentication material for several Active Directory accounts without ever authenticating, simply by requesting authentication-server replies for accounts flagged 'Do not require Kerberos pre-authentication.' Which remediation BEST addresses the root cause?
c: Reset the krbtgt account credential twice to invalidate any forged tickets in circulation
Convert the affected accounts to managed service accounts with automatically rotated passwords
Re-enable Kerberos pre-authentication on the flagged accounts and protect any unavoidable exceptions with long random passwords
Shorten ticket lifetimes and tighten clock synchronization tolerances across the domain

q: An assessor connects to the corporate directory server without presenting any credentials and downloads every employee's username, email address, and group memberships. The directory already enforces LDAPS for all connections. What should the security manager require FIRST?
c: Disable anonymous binds so every directory query requires an authenticated and authorized connection
Migrate clients from simple binds to StartTLS so credentials are protected in transit
Store directory password attributes with a salted, memory-hard hashing algorithm
Enable directory auditing to record which entries each connecting client reads

q: A media company is building an app for smart televisions that have no keyboard and cannot present a browser login form. Users should authorize the TV app from their phones without ever typing credentials on the television. Which OAuth 2.0 flow BEST fits this requirement?
c: Authorization code flow with PKCE executed in a browser on the television itself
Device authorization grant, where the television displays a short code the user enters and approves on a second device
Resource owner password credentials grant, letting the television collect the username and password directly
Client credentials grant using an application identity provisioned to the television

q: A mobile banking app issues short-lived access tokens alongside long-lived refresh tokens. Threat modeling shows a refresh token stolen from a compromised device could silently maintain account access for months. Which control BEST limits this exposure while preserving the seamless login experience?
c: Shorten access token lifetime further so any stolen token expires within minutes
Require the password again whenever a new access token must be issued
Validate audience and issuer claims on every token presented to the API
Rotate the refresh token at each use and revoke the whole token family if a superseded token is ever replayed

q: Attackers email employees a link to a convincingly named third-party application that requests OAuth permissions to 'read your files and mailbox.' Several users click Accept, and the attacker's application retains access even after those users change their passwords. Which response BEST prevents recurrence?
c: Require administrative review before third-party applications receive delegated permissions, allowing only vetted publishers and scopes
Enforce multifactor authentication for all users so their credentials cannot be captured by the phishing site
Shorten single sign-on session lifetimes so any attacker session expires within hours
Block the sending domains at the email gateway and schedule refresher phishing awareness training

q: Employees authenticate with passwords plus app-generated one-time codes. A phishing campaign lures users to a reverse-proxy site that relays the credentials and codes to the real portal in real time, capturing the resulting sessions. Which change BEST prevents this attack from succeeding?
c: Issue hardware one-time-password fobs in place of the authenticator app codes
Lengthen the one-time codes and reduce their validity window to thirty seconds
Deploy phishing-resistant authenticators whose cryptographic response is bound to the legitimate site's origin
Block newly registered domains at the web proxy and train employees to verify URLs before logging in

q: A year after rolling out passkeys, a company still allows password-plus-SMS login 'for users who lose their devices.' Phishing reports show attackers now simply direct victims to the fallback login page. What is the BEST way to address this weakness?
c: Rate-limit the fallback login page and add bot detection to slow automated credential abuse
Convert the fallback into a monitored, identity-proofed account recovery process instead of an always-available alternate login
Add push-notification approval to the fallback flow so users can deny attempts they did not initiate
Mandate passkeys for administrators only and formally accept the residual risk for standard users

q: A manufacturer pilots fingerprint authentication on the shop floor. Several long-tenured machinists cannot register usable prints because of worn or scarred fingertips, though registered users authenticate reliably. Which metric should the evaluation team examine, and what does it imply for the rollout?
c: The false rejection rate, which measures how often legitimate enrolled users are denied
The crossover error rate, which identifies the tuning point where the error curves intersect
The false acceptance rate, which measures how often impostors are wrongly granted access
The failure-to-enroll rate, which shows the strategy must provide an alternative authenticator for workers the sensor cannot register

q: A defense contractor wants fingerprint verification for facility access, but the workers' council objects to any central database of biometric templates that could be breached or repurposed. Which design BEST addresses the objection while keeping biometric assurance?
c: Store each worker's template only on a smart card that performs the match locally, so no central repository of biometric data exists
Encrypt the central template database and tightly restrict administrative access to it
Switch to facial recognition, which can be captured passively and feels less intrusive
Protect stored templates with the salted hashing methods used for passwords

q: Physical security reviews show the same badge recording two consecutive entries to the data center with no intervening exit, suggesting employees are passing one badge back through the door for a colleague. Which control MOST directly addresses this behavior?
c: A mantrap vestibule that admits only one person for each authentication cycle
Anti-passback logic that refuses a badge re-entry until a matching exit has been recorded
Continuously monitored CCTV cameras covering the data center entrance and corridor
Longer retention of badge-reader logs to support future investigations

q: A company migrates servers into a shared colocation facility where the provider controls building entry and dozens of other tenants access the same data hall. Which measure BEST protects the company's equipment from other tenants who are legitimately inside the room?
c: Contract terms requiring the provider to escort all visitors while they are inside the data hall
Provider-operated CCTV coverage of the aisles with footage available on request
A locked cage or cabinet around the company's racks, with keys or credentials held only by its own staff
Full-disk encryption on every server the company hosts at the facility

q: An electric utility's around-the-clock control room uses one always-logged-on operator console because the vendor software cannot switch users quickly and regulators prioritize immediate operator response. Security policy requires individual accountability for all system access. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Enforce unique operator logons at every shift change and require operators to absorb the switching delay
Approve a permanent exception for the control room and formally accept the reduced accountability
Launch an emergency project to replace the vendor platform with one that supports rapid user switching
Document a time-bound exception with compensating controls (badge-controlled entry, shift rosters, cameras) and require user switching in the next upgrade

q: A payroll database can be queried only between 07:00 and 19:00 on weekdays and only through the payroll application's front end; direct connections are refused even for valid accounts. Which access control approach do these restrictions illustrate?
c: Context-dependent access control, which evaluates when and how access is attempted before allowing it
Content-dependent access control, which filters what is returned based on the sensitivity of the records
Discretionary access control, because the payroll data owner chose to impose the restrictions
Mandatory access control, because individual users are unable to override the restrictions

q: After a rogue administrator deleted the backup catalog, the company decides that any purge of backup archives must require two authorized storage administrators to act together at the same time. Which principle is being implemented?
c: Separation of duties, because the task is divided between two different job functions
Dual control, because two authorized people must participate simultaneously for the action to proceed
Least privilege, because each administrator alone holds insufficient rights to purge archives
Job rotation, because no single administrator retains permanent control of the backup function

q: Quarterly access reviews keep discovering users who were added to the domain administrators group months earlier without approval. The IAM team wants to close the gap between an unauthorized grant and its discovery. Which control BEST achieves this?
c: Shorten the access review cycle from quarterly to monthly so discrepancies surface sooner
Require line managers to attest to their teams' privileged access during each campaign
Alert in real time on privileged group membership changes and reconcile every change against an approved request
Move administrator access to just-in-time checkout so no one retains standing group membership

q: Each regional office of a bank maintains its own user accounts and permission standards on local servers. Audits find the same job title holds broad rights in one region and almost none in another, and terminations are missed at smaller sites. Which change BEST addresses these findings?
c: Deploy single sign-on so employees authenticate once to reach systems in every region
Delegate broader administrative authority to the information technology lead in each region
Mandate that all regions configure the same password complexity and lockout baseline
Centralize account and permission administration under one team enforcing uniform enterprise-wide standards

q: The ERP enforces separation of duties within its own module, yet an internal fraud succeeded because one employee could create vendors in the procurement system and approve payments in a separate treasury application. Which improvement BEST prevents recurrence?
c: Define toxic entitlement combinations in the identity governance platform and check every request across all connected systems before granting access
Enable dynamic separation of duties in the ERP so no user can approve a transaction they initiated there
Expand quarterly recertification so each manager reviews their employees' entitlements system by system
Configure mutually exclusive roles inside each application so conflicting duties cannot combine within it

q: Help desk staff provision each new hire by copying the entitlements of 'a similar existing employee.' Audits show new analysts routinely start with rights their peers accumulated over years of transfers and projects. Which change BEST fixes this practice?
c: Require each new hire's manager to review and confirm the granted access within the first ninety days
Provision new hires from approved role definitions that map entitlements to the job, rather than from another employee's profile
Schedule periodic entitlement reviews to strip unused rights from all existing analysts
Reduce the automatically granted birthright baseline so every new account starts with fewer defaults

q: A company closes an acquisition and 3,000 acquired employees need day-one access to the parent's HR and collaboration platforms. Directory consolidation will take at least a year. Which approach BEST provides access now while preserving lifecycle accuracy?
c: Bulk-create accounts in the parent directory for all acquired employees and distribute the new credentials
Synchronize the acquired company's accounts and password hashes into the parent directory as an interim measure
Federate the environments so the acquired company's identity provider authenticates its employees to the parent's applications
Provide VPN access into the parent network and create local accounts on each application the employees need

q: A hospital's 802.1X deployment exempts badge printers and infusion pumps by authenticating their MAC addresses. A red team spoofs a printer's MAC address from a conference-room jack and reaches the clinical VLAN. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Configure alerts whenever an authorized MAC address appears on an unexpected switch port
Review the MAC allow list quarterly and promptly remove entries for retired devices
Permit only certificate-based authentication and retire every device that cannot support it
Use certificate authentication for capable devices and confine the remaining MAC-authenticated devices to tightly restricted network segments

q: In a microservices platform, services authorize calls from peers based on source IP ranges. After a container compromise, the attacker reached internal APIs simply because the calls originated inside the cluster. Which change BEST addresses the weakness?
c: Give each workload a cryptographic identity and require mutually authenticated TLS with per-service authorization policies
Tighten the allow lists from subnet ranges to the individual IP addresses of each pod
Front the internal APIs with a gateway that requires a shared API key from calling services
Encrypt east-west traffic with TLS so internal calls cannot be intercepted or modified

q: A company's forty in-house applications each hardcode their own entitlement checks. Rules drift apart, audits require sampling every codebase, and a regulatory change takes months to reflect everywhere. Which architectural approach BEST addresses these problems?
c: Standardize every application on a shared authorization library maintained by the platform team
Externalize decisions to a central policy engine that applications query at runtime, with policies versioned and audited in one place
Route all traffic through the single sign-on gateway and have it grant or deny each application at login
Consolidate entitlements into directory groups that each application reads to make its own decisions

q: An audit finds 9,000 accounts belonging to workers who left over the past decade; the accounts were disabled on departure and never touched again. What does good identity lifecycle practice call for?
c: Keep the accounts disabled forever, since deleting them would erase the historical audit trail
Delete all of the accounts immediately, because the owners no longer need any access
Retain disabled accounts for a defined period for investigations and data transfer, then delete them on a documented schedule
Remove the accounts' entitlements but keep them enabled so mail forwarding and delegation continue

q: A cloud operations team manages hundreds of Linux servers whose authorized_keys files contain years of accumulated public keys, including some belonging to engineers who left long ago. Which approach BEST brings this access under lifecycle control?
c: Deploy a scheduled scan that inventories every authorized_keys file and reports keys not matched to a current employee
Require passphrases on all private keys and mandate that engineers rotate their key pairs annually
Restrict SSH to a hardened bastion host that records every administrative session
Issue short-lived SSH certificates from an authority tied to the identity provider, so access expires automatically and follows joiner-leaver events

q: During an incident, responders find that every workstation shares the same local administrator password, letting the attacker move laterally across the fleet with a single credential dump. Which control BEST prevents this technique in the future?
c: Automatically randomize every machine's local administrator password and vault it centrally with audited retrieval
Disable local administrator accounts and have support staff log on with domain administrator credentials instead
Apply stricter length and complexity requirements to the standard local administrator password
Rename the local administrator account on every workstation to a value attackers cannot guess

q: Badge readers control entry to a pharmaceutical company's server room, and recorded CCTV covers the corridor. During a walkthrough, an auditor finds the door propped open with a fire extinguisher while technicians carry equipment in and out; the badge logs show only normal individual entries. Which control would BEST give the security team real-time awareness of this condition?
c: Install a mantrap vestibule so only one person can pass through the entrance at a time
Enable anti-passback rules on the badge system for the server room readers
Add a dedicated camera covering the door and extend the CCTV retention period
Install a door-position sensor that raises a held-open alarm at the security monitoring station

q: A logistics enterprise exchanges federated identities with roughly forty partner carriers. The IAM team reports that maintaining a separate SAML trust with each partner — metadata exchange, signing-certificate renewals, and per-partner legal agreements — now consumes most of its capacity, and about five new partners join every quarter. Which approach BEST reduces this burden while preserving federated access?
c: Participate in a federation broker so each organization maintains a single trust with the hub
Provision internally managed directory accounts for all partner carrier users
Require every partner carrier to authenticate its users against the enterprise's own identity provider
Synchronize partner directory passwords into the enterprise directory on a recurring schedule

q: An unattended nightly batch job in a company's integration tier must call a partner's REST API that is protected by OAuth 2.0. A developer proposes configuring a senior analyst's username and password into the job so it can obtain tokens. Which OAuth 2.0 approach is MOST appropriate for this integration?
c: Authorization code flow with PKCE initiated through a browser redirect
Resource owner password credentials grant using the analyst's account
Client credentials grant using the batch job's own registered client identity and secret
Implicit grant so tokens are returned to the job without a code exchange

q: SIEM alerts show that an ERP application's service account has been performing interactive desktop logons on several administrator workstations. Investigation confirms no compromise: administrators had learned the password and were using the account for routine troubleshooting because it already held broad rights. After the credential is rotated, which control BEST prevents this misuse from recurring?
c: Enroll the service account in multifactor authentication
Apply a directory policy that denies the account interactive and remote logon, permitting service logon only
Shorten the service account's password expiration interval
Add the account to the quarterly privileged access recertification campaign

q: During a design review of a new customer portal, a developer states that the registration page is secure because a CAPTCHA was added for authentication. How should the security consultant BEST characterize what the CAPTCHA actually provides?
c: It verifies the registrant's claimed identity before the account is created
It deters automated bulk account creation but does not authenticate any individual
It acts as a second authentication factor alongside the user's password
It authorizes the newly created account to access portal resources
